method: Manual public-source qualification of the 50-candidate seed list. SELLABLE requires a documented control or representation, contrary or unresolved observed activity, and a concrete evidence-acquisition path. It is not a finding of wrongdoing.

assessments.control: Nebraska query-purpose law, department release controls and recurring audit requirements.
assessments.observed: A broad outside-access population is reported, but comparable authorization and audit populations are not yet in hand.
assessments.missingProof: SharedNetworks, Network Audit, Event Log and semiannual audit memoranda.

assessments.control: The city reportedly understood the sharing population to be about 80 and said statewide or national sharing was not enabled.
assessments.observed: Network records reportedly identified 459 outside organizations and about 1.6 million searches; the city ended the agreement.
assessments.missingProof: Dated sharing export, full Network Audit, Event Log and vendor incident correspondence.

assessments.control: The contract, data-use assurances and cybersecurity representations remain to be extracted.
assessments.observed: The mayor called for ending the contract; police reportedly reduced shared networks by 149.
assessments.missingProof: Contract, pre/post sharing exports, council packet and audit logs.

assessments.control: California law restricts ALPR disclosure to federal and out-of-state agencies.
assessments.observed: The attorney general alleges repeated sharing with agencies in more than two dozen states despite warnings.
assessments.missingProof: Complaint exhibits, sharing exports, warning correspondence and current policy.

assessments.control: The sheriff disabled National Lookup in 2023 to comply with California law.
assessments.observed: A later audit reportedly found more than 364,000 out-of-state and federal accesses in two months, including 299 immigration-referenced justifications.
assessments.missingProof: Complete audit, configuration history, query population and vendor root-cause report.

assessments.control: California law and SFPD controls prohibit federal and out-of-state ALPR sharing.
assessments.observed: An audit identified nearly 300 improper searches through a regional intelligence-center access path; SFPD cut off access.
assessments.missingProof: Query-level audit, access agreement, approval trail and corrective-action record.

assessments.control: Renton requires a valid case number, authorized investigation and documented justification; its sharing report did not list Border Patrol.
assessments.observed: Network Audit records show two Border Patrol searches of Renton data on June 23, 2025.
assessments.missingProof: Complete Network Audit, purpose fields, access-path configuration and twice-monthly reviews.

assessments.control: Public city messaging said Denver data was not shared with ICE.
assessments.observed: Logs reportedly show more than 1,400 immigration-related searches since June 2024; Denver later ended Flock use.
assessments.missingProof: Logs, access path, approvals, policy and termination review.

assessments.control: Boulder deactivated National Lookup in June 2025 and now describes Colorado-only sharing.
assessments.observed: Earlier audits reportedly show more than 100 Border Patrol searches; one day included Boulder data in 5,438 queries.
assessments.missingProof: Pre/post configuration exports, full audits and authorization for earlier nationwide access.

assessments.control: Tempe audited monthly and reported no internal misuse.
assessments.observed: The city shut down its 33-camera system because prospective misuse risk was considered too high.
assessments.missingProof: Contrary logs or configuration records; cancellation alone is not a variance.

assessments.control: A regular internal-affairs audit supplied the supervisory control.
assessments.observed: The audit flagged possible criminal misuse by an officer, who was placed on leave.
assessments.missingProof: Policy, flagged queries, administrative order and completed investigation.

assessments.control: The sheriff initiated an audit against legitimate-purpose and authorized-use controls.
assessments.observed: The review expanded into multiple firings and resignations after allegedly unrelated searches.
assessments.missingProof: Full audit population, individual findings, policy versions and supervisory history.

assessments.control: A self-initiated account audit supplied the agency's use-control test.
assessments.observed: Three employees resigned after accounts were flagged; the matter was referred for state investigation.
assessments.missingProof: Audit, account histories, referral and policy acknowledgments.

assessments.control: Searches required a legitimate work purpose and truthful justification.
assessments.observed: A former deputy allegedly searched one personal plate 2,055 times using a false planning or traffic justification; charges followed.
assessments.missingProof: Query export, audit methodology, charging affidavit and supervisory alerts.

assessments.control: The deployment depends on the sheriff's ALPR protocol and local approval record.
assessments.observed: The village suspended cameras pending a county-deputy investigation and protocol review.
assessments.missingProof: Sheriff audit, village agreement, council record and suspension correspondence.

assessments.control: The department reportedly had no ALPR-specific policy until after the conduct, then imposed monthly audits.
assessments.observed: A dispatcher allegedly performed 20,292 searches, including 5,369 of one plate, before resigning.
assessments.missingProof: Account audit, prior access policy, alert history and corrective-action documents.

assessments.control: MPD access is restricted to legitimate law-enforcement use and is auditable by user and purpose.
assessments.observed: Multiple reported cases allege personnel repeatedly tracked private individuals for personal reasons.
assessments.missingProof: Account query histories, acknowledgments, audit frequency and disciplinary findings.

assessments.control: Searches required authorized investigative use and accurate case documentation.
assessments.observed: A detective was arrested and terminated after allegedly using unrelated case numbers and false records; the entire system was suspended.
assessments.missingProof: Query export, false entries, affidavit, audit and remedial review.

assessments.control: Policy barred unjustified off-duty access to the controlled investigative resource.
assessments.observed: An internal investigation reportedly substantiated an improper search of a former partner's plate and contributed to a resignation.
assessments.missingProof: Investigative file, query record, policy and supervisor notification trail.

assessments.control: A routine audit tested access against authorized law-enforcement use.
assessments.observed: The audit flagged alleged misuse, an employee resigned and the matter was referred to the state SBI.
assessments.missingProof: Flagged searches, internal review, referral and final findings.

assessments.control: The constitutional question concerns warrantless movement reconstruction across 172 cameras.
assessments.observed: The network has generated extensive histories and litigation, but no discrete control-versus-audit variance is established.
assessments.missingProof: Query/use statistics, retention and access logs; keep the constitutional thesis distinct.

assessments.control: The department limits sharing geographically and requires legitimate purposes plus an audit trail.
assessments.observed: The system was suspended after an officer allegedly used it to track a former partner.
assessments.missingProof: Query history, audit trigger, policy acknowledgments and completed investigation.

assessments.control: State law and Milford policy impose sharing, access, retention and audit restrictions.
assessments.observed: Public material may show a broader reachable network than direct sharing, but the populations are not yet verified as comparable.
assessments.missingProof: Original SharedNetworks and Network Audit exports before stating a numerical variance.

assessments.control: The city debated privacy, security and oversight before declining renewal.
assessments.observed: No contrary access or audit population has been verified.
assessments.missingProof: Original audit records; cancellation alone is not a marketed Red Dot.

assessments.control: The city did not directly authorize federal immigration access and later said it inadvertently joined national sharing.
assessments.observed: Records reportedly show 175 CBP-related searches in one period and 2,097 immigration-labeled searches in a longer window.
assessments.missingProof: Complete audit, configuration history, approval record and vendor notices.

assessments.control: Official settings limited access to California agencies and barred federal/out-of-state sharing.
assessments.observed: The city reported two federal nationwide queries reached its data and suspended the system.
assessments.missingProof: Query details, configuration history and Flock technical incident report.

assessments.control: The city intended California-limited access and did not authorize federal use.
assessments.observed: An audit found multiple federal agencies accessed local data without consent; the contract was terminated.
assessments.missingProof: Complete audit, technical access path, vendor correspondence and termination file.

assessments.control: Los Altos publishes California-only sharing, documented-purpose and audit controls.
assessments.observed: The agency explains that Network Audit appearance does not itself prove access to Los Altos data.
assessments.missingProof: Query-level evidence establishing actual contrary access.

assessments.control: California law and city representations limit federal/out-of-state access.
assessments.observed: Reporting indicates federal access including at least one ICE-related matter across a large deployment.
assessments.missingProof: Original Network Audit, access agreements, policy and approvals.

assessments.control: Berkeley requires a signed agreement and legitimate California law-enforcement purpose.
assessments.observed: No verified contrary access population emerged.
assessments.missingProof: Retain as a control-rich comparison city, not an unresolved variance.

assessments.control: Tiburon requires monthly audits and California-only, non-immigration use.
assessments.observed: The town says audited searches were legitimate and ended sharing with nonresponsive agencies.
assessments.missingProof: This presently appears reconciled; monitor released audits.

assessments.control: Local authorization and purpose limits for the 60-camera deployment remain to be extracted.
assessments.observed: The public sharing footprint reportedly reaches 365 agencies nationwide.
assessments.missingProof: Policy, SharedNetworks, Network Audit and council authorization.

assessments.control: Dallas policy, retention rules and approval record are the required baseline.
assessments.observed: A 2025 audit reportedly contains 63,586 searches; some queries reached 100,000-plus devices across roughly 7,000 networks.
assessments.missingProof: Complete audit separating local searches, nationwide searches and actual Dallas-data access.

assessments.control: Council declined renewal after considering sharing, storage and oversight.
assessments.observed: No specific contrary access or misuse record emerged.
assessments.missingProof: Retain as governance history, not a marketed Red Dot.

assessments.control: Fort Worth operates a large deployment with stated 30-day retention.
assessments.observed: A public request for audit logs exists, but the exports have not been analyzed.
assessments.missingProof: Acquire and analyze Network Audit and sharing configuration.

assessments.control: The sheriff denied abortion-ban enforcement and the search was characterized as a missing-person matter.
assessments.observed: A nationwide search across 83,345 cameras used the reason 'had an abortion'; an affidavit reportedly tied the case to an alleged abortion.
assessments.missingProof: Query record, affidavit, requestor communications, approval and redisclosure trail.

assessments.control: Austin's governance framework and information-sharing rules supply the baseline.
assessments.observed: A city audit identified information-sharing flaws amid a 113-million-scan annual footprint; the contract ended.
assessments.missingProof: Audit workpapers, access population, corrective actions and termination record.

assessments.control: Authorized investigative use and truthful query purposes governed access.
assessments.observed: An officer was indicted on 100 counts after reportedly conducting more than 45,000 searches, including thousands involving a former partner.
assessments.missingProof: Indictment, query export, audit trigger, supervisory history and preservation notices.

assessments.control: Katy states the system is restricted to authorized investigations.
assessments.observed: A former officer was charged after allegedly using Flock for months to track his former wife.
assessments.missingProof: Query history, charging instrument, policy acknowledgement and supervisory audit.

assessments.control: The city system was restricted to authorized law-enforcement use.
assessments.observed: An official review found possible unauthorized use in late 2024 and early 2025; records were preserved and referred.
assessments.missingProof: Preserved logs, findings, referral and policy history.

assessments.control: The inspector general urged enforceable privacy, security and oversight safeguards.
assessments.observed: LAPD halted and ended Flock use after an audit identified control and performance failures, including reported wrongful stops.
assessments.missingProof: Inspector-general audit, error population, hot-list workflow, contract and corrective action.

assessments.control: A class action alleges the nearly 600-camera program lacked legislative authorization and adequate oversight.
assessments.observed: The system reportedly accumulated 1.6 billion scans and shared information with more than 50 agencies, including ICE.
assessments.missingProof: Complaint exhibits, county authorization, sharing agreements, logs and retention controls.

assessments.control: Windsor adopted a local ALPR privacy policy intended to constrain data access and sharing.
assessments.observed: Reported out-of-state access conflicted with that policy; council voted 8-1 to turn off 16 cameras.
assessments.missingProof: Policy, access audit, contract, configuration and council findings.

assessments.control: The town reconsidered based on privacy, records workload, cost and utility.
assessments.observed: Four cameras were removed, but no specific contrary activity has been verified.
assessments.missingProof: An access audit; termination alone is governance history.

assessments.control: Lansing reports quarterly audits and defined authorized uses.
assessments.observed: Council requested termination, but no verified misuse or access variance emerged.
assessments.missingProof: Quarterly audits before promotion.

assessments.control: Officials halted a proposed deployment and later banned ALPRs on constitutional and privacy grounds.
assessments.observed: This is a policy rejection, not an operational discrepancy.
assessments.missingProof: Evidence from a prior live deployment, if any.

assessments.control: Virginia law limits sharing to in-state members and imposes retention and audit requirements.
assessments.observed: Staunton terminated after security concerns while officials acknowledged reliance on other agencies to audit their own users.
assessments.missingProof: Network Audits, termination analysis, contract and post-law configuration.

assessments.control: Cambridge deactivated 16 cameras and ended the contract, requiring vendor work to cease.
assessments.observed: Flock technicians installed two additional cameras afterward without city awareness under an uncancelled work order.
assessments.missingProof: Work order, installation logs, termination notice, account status and incident response.

assessments.control: Eugene opted out of nationwide lookup and represented Oregon-only access.
assessments.observed: A later full-period audit found federal-agency searches in May and June 2025; the city ended the contract.
assessments.missingProof: Full audit, configuration timeline, federal queries and vendor explanation.

assessments.control: Monroe publishes deployment, cost, locations and Snohomish County-only sharing.
assessments.observed: No verified contrary access or misuse emerged.
assessments.missingProof: Network Audits; otherwise use as a clean baseline.
